source: Aria Networks — Closing conversation: Deep Networking and token economics; Aria vs Arista's rise in the cloud era; NeoCloud and accelerator vendors
summary: Elon Musk's Colossus cluster success (100,000 XPUs coherent) was driven by extreme focus on networking quality
summary_extended: Baker recounts the anecdote of Elon Musk personally re-plugging every cable at the Colossus 1 cluster as evidence that networking quality is the binding constraint on large-scale AI cluster performance. Musk's hands-on intervention enabled 100,000 coherent XPUs at a time when industry consensus held that 40,000 was the ceiling given the limitations of then-current switch technology (Tomahawk 5). Baker uses this story to argue structurally that networking — not compute — is the critical bottleneck determining how large a coherent cluster can scale. The investment implication is that companies providing high-quality networking solutions for AI datacenters are disproportionately important, though this specific anecdote does not name or clearly imply any single publicly traded networking beneficiary. NVDA is not the subject of or a direct beneficiary of this thesis, which is about networking architecture constraints rather than GPU compute demand.
detail: Baker recounts that Musk personally re-plugged every cable at Colossus 1 because he identified the network as the most important part of the cluster.
